source.publication: Publication 120 Retirement Income (December 2025), with the 2025 IL-1040 Instructions and Form IL-1040
source.section: Pub 120 PDF page 2 'What retirement income may I subtract', PDF page 3 'What federally taxed income may I not subtract'; Form IL-1040 Line 5; Instructions PDF page 7, Line 5; Form IL-1040 PDF page 1, Lines 1-19; Instructions PDF page 8, Lines 10-12; rate Instructions PDF page 1; Line 10a chart and Income Exceptions, Instructions PDF page 8

worked: Federal AGI = IL government pension (person 0) 30,000.00 + private pension (person 1) 20,000.00 + IRA distribution (person 0) 40,000.00 + employer plan distribution (person 1) 10,000.00 + taxable Social Security (of 40,000.00 gross) 34,000.00 + interest 10,000.00 + dividends 20,000.00 + short-term gains 7,700.00 + long-term gains 20,000.00 = 191,700.00. Federal taxable income = 191,700.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 - additional amount for 2 person(s) 65 or older 3,200.00 = 157,000.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Illinois starts from federal AGI). Form IL-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 191,700.00. Line 2 federally tax-exempt interest 0.00. Line 3 other additions 0.00. Line 4 = 191,700.00. Line 5 IL government pension 30,000.00 + private pension 20,000.00 + IRA distribution 40,000.00 + employer plan distribution 10,000.00 + federally taxed Social Security 34,000.00 = 134,000.00. Lines 6 and 7 0.00. Line 8 = 134,000.00. Line 9 base income = 191,700.00 - 134,000.00 = 57,700.00. Income Exceptions: federal AGI 191,700.00 is not greater than 500,000.00, so the allowance stands. Line 10a 5,700.00. Line 10b 2,000.00 (2 box(es) x 1,000.00). Lines 10c and 10d 0.00. Line 10 = 7,700.00. Line 11 net income = 57,700.00 - 7,700.00 = 50,000.00. Line 12 tax = 50,000.00 x 4.95% = 2,475.0000. Lines 13-18 0.00 (no credits in the projection). Line 19 state income tax = 2,475.00. Interest, dividends and both kinds of gains take the one flat rate; Illinois has no capital gains rate of its own.
